text:
Philip Broberg is playing more than ever, nearly 26 minutes a night over his last ten games and above 28 in two of them. He's on the ice for 54% of St. Louis's power-play time after 28% last season, and he has 13 points in 18 games, already more than a third of last season's 34. The Hockey News pointed to him as proof that paying young defensemen with upside works, and The Hockey Writers named him a Blues standout of the week.

The production outruns the play underneath it, though. St. Louis gets just 45% of the expected goals at five on five with him on, seven points worse than without him, and the Blues have scored 7.8 more goals than expected while he's out there. That luck is doing a lot of the work on his point total, which sits well above our range.

Evolving-Hockey liked him a lot last season (20th of 215 defensemen, plus 4 goals just from drawing penalties), and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking put his home-plate chances in the 95th percentile among defensemen. The talent is there. Watch the five-on-five share: the minutes have grown faster than the results.
headline: Broberg has become St. Louis's top-minute defenseman
